- Titel: Brief von Lotte Zweig an Hannah Altmann [13. März 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.105

- Datum: 13.3.1941
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 3 Scans

pages.transcription:
Taft Hotel                                Newhaven, March 13th, 1941.

Dear Hanna,

Finally your letter Nr. 3 from Febr. 8th has arrived,
delayed because you had written 18th Street 48 East instead of
18 East 48th Street. You were of course right not to give Hans
any more money after the first 35£ which after all is a considerable
sum. I am terribly sorry that through the vague expressions in my
letter to him he got the impression that you could dispose of Stefan's
money quite freely and that you had the disagreeable task of refusing
him any more. I have written him again to-day telling him quite
clearly that another £20 is the utmost we can give him until August.
This is Stefan's instruction to you which I transmit that you may
give Hans once more £20 and that then - with these 55£ - he has nothing
to expect from us until at least August. By that time, I hope, he will
have found a good job.

Otherwise there is nothing to report. We had a nice
letter from Eva, a special effort on her part for style, and the
funny part about it is that it sounded curiously like one of Manfred's
letters in style. - I got up to-day for the first time after my 'flu
and hope that poor Stefan soon gets his secretary back.

Best love, kisses,
Lotte

Dear Hannah, this is the first letter to be able
to write since 10 days. After her heavy astma-attack
she has a very bad flu and is still in bed; I hope she can go up tomorrow.
Of cause it is not nice to have this in an American Hotel which has a
resemblance of {resemblance} with a railway-station, no personal touch and interest. We
has only a doctor from an other century and no else in this little town.
And we are both so tired of this nomadic life as you cannot imagine. But
the first thing is that she gets fit again and later we shall see what to do
next - all is uncertain in those times. I am only glad that we can rely
on Mr. Klaeffer for Eva, as it will not be possible to see her next week and
perhaps before April. It Lotte feels better we have still to go for two days
to Baltimore, for one day at least to Newyork. But time flies! - I wrote
you about the birth-certificates and forgot to tell you, that it will be
perhaps better to tear them through Ingram as this proves that I want them
for a legal matter, but if you have already done it, there is no harm.
Kindest regards to you all
Stefan Zweig
pages.notes: Der Text am linken Rand (vertikal geschrieben) lautet: 'Lotte asks you to keep the letter to her brother [?] as she does not know his actual adress.' Der Brief besteht aus einem maschinengeschriebenen Teil (Lotte) und einem handschriftlichen Teil (Stefan Zweig). Die Einfügung '{resemblance}' wurde im Original über das Wort 'resemblance' geschrieben, das bereits im Text stand.
Rückseite des Dokuments, zeigt den durchscheinenden Text der Vorderseite (spiegelverkehrt).
Farbskala/Grauskala für Archivierung. Überlagert den Text des Briefes.

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar. Die handschriftlichen Ergänzungen und der handschriftliche Teil von Stefan Zweig sind klar identifizierbar.
